subject_entity.notes: Tertullian's treatise on baptism c. 198-200; earliest surviving monograph on baptism; describes trinitarian formula, sponsors, and recommends delaying baptism of children.

object_entity.notes: First major Latin Christian author; active in Carthage c. 195–220. Wrote at least 31 works spanning apologetics, anti-heretical polemic, and moral discipline. Coined 'trinitas' and 'tres personae una substantia'. Defender of apostolic succession, rule of faith, incarnation, and bodily resurrection. Later attracted to Montanist rigorism c. 207; teacher of Cyprian by doctrinal influence.

evidence.notes: Delay of baptism recommended for little children; let them become Christians when able to know Christ

passage.excerpt: And so, according to the circumstances and disposition, and even age, of each individual, the delay of baptism is preferable; principally, however, in the case of little children. For why is it necessary — if baptism itself be not so necessary — that the sponsors likewise should be thrust into danger? Let them come, then, while they are growing up; let them come while they are learning, while they are being taught whither to come; let them become Christians when they have become able to know Christ.
passage.notes: Recommends delaying baptism of children; earliest explicit argument against routine infant baptism
